title: 3740. Minimum Distance Between Three Equal Elements I

examples.explanation: The minimum distance is achieved by the good tuple (0, 2, 3). (0, 2, 3) is a good tuple because nums[0] == nums[2] == nums[3] == 1. Its distance is abs(0 - 2) + abs(2 - 3) + abs(3 - 0) = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6.

The minimum distance is achieved by the good tuple (2, 4, 6). (2, 4, 6) is a good tuple because nums[2] == nums[4] == nums[6] == 2. Its distance is abs(2 - 4) + abs(4 - 6) + abs(6 - 2) = 2 + 2 + 4 = 8.
There are no good tuples. Therefore, the answer is -1.
